mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2% over two consecutive quarters signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDPC1 below its previous quarter's value for two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDP declines.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of four consecutive monthly INDPRO declines below the 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS over the same month indicates increased housing demand with reduced savings, suggesting consumer leverage expansion, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND RSAFS < previous month in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST rises and RSAFS falls in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in FEDFUNDS below 1% while CPIAUCSL rises above 2% year-over-year signals an unexpected loosening amid inflation, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to anticipated policy reversal.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 0.25% in one month AND CPIAUCSL > 2% YoY in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS drops sharply and CPIAUCSL exceeds 2% YoY in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: PAYEMS increases steadily for five consecutive months while UNRATE remains below 5%, indicating robust job creation without wage inflation, which historically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for five consecutive months AND UNRATE < 5% in all five months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during five consecutive months of rising PAYEMS with UNRATE below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: GDPC1 grows above 3% quarter-over-quarter with no concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 2% month-over-month, indicating real demand expansion without inflation, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ growth > 3% AND CPIAUCSL MoM <= 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 grows > 3% QoQ and CPIAUCSL does not exceed 2% MoM.
